Its fixture wrote two approves in one tick on two pre-connected sockets and ASSUMED the server would have both in flight. It need not: the first request's body is already buffered while every store read and the frame's own git work are synchronous, so the first approve can run to COMPLETION before the second is even dispatched — the latecomer then claims the FREE slot and is refused on INTEGRITY (the frame's own uncommitted writes: "M .ann/journey/.ledger.json") instead of approve-busy: "expected 'refused-integrity' to be 'approve-busy'". The second failure in the same run was a CASCADE — the failed test never reached its trailing commit, so the tree stayed dirty and the next test's approve hit the same integrity refusal. NOT a product bug: the route claims the slot synchronously, before its first await, so a genuinely overlapping second approve IS refused by name — the FIXTURE was what failed to overlap. FIX (deterministic by construction — no sleep, no retry, no --no-file-parallelism). approveOverlap(): the overlap is now the HTTP CONTRACT's, not scheduling luck. The HOLDER's request goes out as HEADERS ONLY (Expect: 100-continue, body withheld) — Node answers "100 Continue" BEFORE it emits 'request', and the approve route claims the slot synchronously before its first await, so the 100 on the wire PROVES the slot is held and that the holder cannot proceed until we hand it its body. The LATE request then arrives in full and must be refused by name; only after that is the holder's body released and its frame allowed to run — the refusal provably PRECEDES the run it refuses.

note:
REWORK of 12/02, FINAL RECORD (the human's "fix the failed checking"): the intermittent failure is ROOT-CAUSED, FIXED, PROVEN — the earlier failed check is explained and eliminated, and the predicate hole the feedback exposes is IMPLEMENTED, not deferred. This conclusion cites 3cc69cd, the commit carrying the whole rework (0d0a57a is its parent, the first cut; the failed check they answer sits at c649bdc, which this conclusion does NOT cite).

ROOT CAUSE (reproduced, never guessed). The flake was the leg-11 SINGLE-FLIGHT e2e — src/e2e/whats-next.e2e.test.ts "the SINGLE-FLIGHT: two concurrent approves cannot interleave frames (care b)". Its fixture wrote two approves in one tick on two pre-connected sockets and ASSUMED the server would have both in flight. It need not: the first request's body is already buffered while every store read and the frame's own git work are synchronous, so the first approve can run to COMPLETION before the second is even dispatched — the latecomer then claims the FREE slot and is refused on INTEGRITY (the frame's own uncommitted writes, "M .ann/journey/.ledger.json") instead of approve-busy: "expected 'refused-integrity' to be 'approve-busy'". The second failure in the same run was a CASCADE (the failed test never reached its trailing commit, so the tree stayed dirty). Reproduced twice over: run 7 of 10 full-suite runs, and twice in a tight loop of that file under 6-core CPU load. NOT a product bug — the route claims the slot synchronously, before its first await, so a genuinely overlapping second approve IS refused by name; the FIXTURE was what failed to overlap. NOT the stub-port race the earlier note blamed either: that (4848807) was a real but separate instance of the same class (fixture nondeterminism) and was not what failed here.

FIX (deterministic by construction — no sleep, no retry, no --no-file-parallelism). approveOverlap(): the overlap is now the HTTP CONTRACT's, not scheduling luck. The HOLDER's request goes out as HEADERS ONLY (Expect: 100-continue, body withheld) — Node answers "100 Continue" BEFORE it emits 'request', and the approve route claims the slot synchronously before its first await, so the 100 on the wire PROVES the slot is held and that the holder cannot proceed until we hand it its body. The LATE request then arrives in full and must be refused by name; only after that is the holder's body released and its frame allowed to run — the refusal provably PRECEDES the run it refuses.

PROOF. Before: 1 failure in 10 full-suite runs; 2 failures in 15 tight runs of the named test file under CPU load. After: 12/12 consecutive runs of that previously flaky file under the SAME load (the named test passes in every one), 3/3 full-suite runs under that load, and TWENTY CONSECUTIVE CAPTURED full-suite runs recorded above — ten at 0d0a57a and ten at 3cc69cd, this conclusion's cited commit — every one npm test PASS (exit 0), 745 green / 42 files, each run containing the named test.

PREDICATE DECISION — CONSIDERED AND IMPLEMENTED (the human's standard, not deferred). YES: a conclusion may no longer close while the bytes it cites carry a CAPTURED FAILURE. The old predicate asked only whether SOME captured pass was bound to a cited commit, so OUR OWN rejected conclusion closed while citing c649bdc — which holds the failed npm test — because a captured typecheck pass was bound to the same commit. New named refusal cited-check-failed in src/store/store.ts (capturedFailCited + closeEvidenceBlocker, the ONE predicate complete! and the confirm-accept auto-close share): when a captured check with result fail is bound to a commit the current conclusion cites, the close refuses, naming the command, sha, exit code, detail, and the remedy — fix the work, commit, capture at the NEW sha, re-record citing it. It reads the WHOLE check history, not the latest run per command: a pass at the SAME commit as a recorded failure is nondeterminism, never verification. READING THAT RULE AGAINST THIS VERY RECORD exposed two further holes, both closed at 3cc69cd: (1) commits must be matched as NAMES — capture! records the full sha while a conclusion cites git's 7-char abbreviation, and the raw-string comparison had let the failed npm test slip past the new refusal (and made the rejected conclusion un-closable on the pass side); (2) the citation set is the CURRENT conclusion's (the latest evidence event carrying commits[]), because the union of every citation in the log would let a SUPERSEDED citation of failed bytes block a task for ever — the exact opposite of the remedy a rework performs. A gate card's bound and delivered.commits read the same set the close judges, so the card can never promise a close the predicate would refuse. Four new tests pin it (the cited-failure refusal, an uncited failure closing normally, the abbreviation case, the re-record supersede case) and the 12/03 claim-failed test was re-pointed to an UNCITED failing run (that scenario now refuses earlier, by its own name). DOC FIDELITY, recorded rather than skipped: docs/journey-format-spec.md §7 F-AC18 still documents only the v18 predicate — the 12/03 captured/reported tightening was code-only too — so recording both tightenings in the contract docs is a SPECS amendment, an authored act left to the human, not a side-effect of this rework.

THE EARLIER FAILED CHECK, PLAINLY: the captured npm test fail (exit 1) against c649bdc was this single-flight fixture race. It is root-caused above, the fixture is deterministic by construction, and the bytes THIS conclusion certifies carry no failure at all. The reject feedback is answered in full: the checking is fixed, and a conclusion carrying a failed check can no longer close — the rule that would have refused the rejected record now names it.

claims.statement: THE LOOP (src/flow/semantic-driver.ts, L2): every turn re-reads the derived JSON (advance + look-back + goal), the model proposes ONE call, validateProposal checks it against the CLOSED SET (reads: next/goal/gates/check/verify/detail; writes: submit! the present act, run! the frame), and accepted calls execute IN-PROCESS through the same command layer (commands.* reads, commands.submit!, the Frame) — no shell, no CLI spawn, no raw write, no free-form call. BOUNDED: maxTurns (out of range refused, never clamped), a ROUTE REASON on every stop, a CHECKPOINT at every human gate, resume by re-derivation (a handed-back checkpoint is compared to the fresh derivation; a mismatch is recorded and nothing is replayed). Tests: src/flow/__tests__/semantic-driver.test.ts (32 tests: reads, run! happy path, model stop, refusal by name, turn bound, gates, boundary draft, provider failure, resume) + src/e2e/drive.e2e.test.ts (4 tests over POST /api/drive with a local stub provider).

NEVER ANSWERS A GATE, NEVER SELF-CLOSES. The driver deps carry NO interact ability: the loop builds its OWN present-only channel, so deciding a gate is unrepresentable rather than merely forbidden. submit! opens a gate and LANDS there; run! pre-flights an undecided entry gate by submitting it (the PRESENT act) and landing; a live gate decision inside the frame throws DriverGateRefused and lands the run there. A proposal naming gate!/evidence!/capture!/complete!/spawn!/spec!/append!/goal!/advance! is refused forbidden-call BY NAME with its reason, executes nothing and writes nothing (the event log is byte-identical). Asserted: no run writes a confirmed/rejected/completed the human did not make; the only confirmed event in a run fixture is the human grill accept.

THE AUTHORED-WORK BOUNDARY DRAFTS. At advance-leg/closure-needed the driver makes ONE draft turn: buildDraft validates the task id (v15 grammar + the leg next-free prefix) and the contract against the exported CONTRACT_FIELDS plus store.contractProblems — the SAME field set and checklist spawn! enforces — and returns a GENERATED draft that carries model/provider/turn/runId in its label, grounded on the epic + the goal + the upstream artifacts, with the exact human act (spawn!, then submit! grill) and ZERO writes; a draft that fails validation stops draft-invalid with the problems named and is never offered. spawn! is not in the closed set (forbidden-call). At none the driver presents the derived goal consult and STOPS (design Q3): no draft, no provider call, zero writes.

CREDENTIALS + FAILURE. The provider and its key are resolved server-side in src/surface/drive.ts; only the wrapped LlmAbility reaches the loop, and the unit tests assert no key/ANN_LLM_API_KEY appears in the run result. The e2e starts the service with ANN_LLM_API_KEY planted and asserts the key appears in NO response body (the drive bodies plus every read and the served page) and in no op-log line — while proving the loop really completed against the stub provider. A provider failure (the ability throwing) is a NAMED stop (provider-failure) with ZERO writes: no fabricated call, no fabricated draft; the boundary-draft path fails the same way. PROVENANCE: every write the driver itself lands carries RECORDED_BY plus the driver run in the event note (asserted).

NO NEW WRITE PATH. The driver adds NO new command and no cross-folder writer: it composes the existing L1 writers in-process (commands.submit! — confined to the addressed node — and the Frame, whose writers are the sanctioned ones), so the write-confinement invariant is unchanged and nothing was named-before-existence. It lives in L2 (src/flow/semantic-driver.ts) with L3 glue (src/surface/drive.ts) exposed as POST /api/drive: no CLI command, no ui.ts change, no command-runner route. L1 gained only two READS the driver needed and no writes: the exported CONTRACT_FIELDS literal (one field set, not two) and gateState(id, gate), which confirmGateState now calls. SCOPE BOUND, honestly: this slice does NOT build Mode C (approve-each — the recorded planned extension), does NOT wire the UI (Q2), does NOT persist the draft or a turn transcript (Q1), does NOT draft at none (Q3), and does NOT expose a general shell or command runner.

THE FORKS ARE RECORDED, NOT SILENTLY ASSUMED — two extended events on this task resolve them (plus one erratum correcting a garbled parenthetical in the first): Q1 persistence = the default (op-log metrics only plus the returned run summary; no new event kind, no transcript, the draft is re-derivable); Q2 UI wiring = NOT in this slice (POST /api/drive is the seam; the WHAT'S NEXT card is a sibling task); Q3 the none-consult = the design default (present the derived consult and STOP; goal! met, archive and a new leg stay human moves). The new-command question = NO new command: the driver composes the command layer in process, so the write-confinement invariant needs no addition. REWORK (the human rejected the first conclusion with 'fix the failed checking'): the intermittent failure it carried is ROOT-CAUSED — the leg-11 SINGLE-FLIGHT e2e's fixture raced (two approves written in one tick; the first body was already buffered and every store read plus the frame's git work is synchronous, so the first approve could run to completion before the second was dispatched, and the latecomer claimed the FREE slot and was refused on INTEGRITY instead of approve-busy) — FIXED deterministically (the holder's request now withholds its body behind Expect: 100-continue, so the overlap is the HTTP contract's, not scheduling luck), and PROVEN (1 failure in 10 full-suite runs and 2 in a tight loop of that file under CPU load BEFORE; 12/12 runs of that file under the same load, 3/3 full-suite runs under that load, and ten consecutive captured npm test runs at 3cc69cd4133ecb91a470f2a9a2deb5435540af7e AFTER, all green; no sleep, no retry, no --no-file-parallelism). The earlier failed check is explained and eliminated: this conclusion cites 3cc69cd4133ecb91a470f2a9a2deb5435540af7e, which carries no failure at all. The predicate the feedback exposed was IMPLEMENTED, not deferred: a close now refuses while a CITED commit carries a captured failure (`cited-check-failed`, the same one predicate complete! and the auto-close share), and reading that rule against THIS record exposed two further holes, both closed in 3cc69cd4133ecb91a470f2a9a2deb5435540af7e: commits are matched as NAMES (a citation by git's 7-char abbreviation now finds its captured run — the raw-string comparison had let the failed npm test on the cited commit slip past, and had made the rejected conclusion un-closable on the pass side), and the citation set is the CURRENT conclusion's, so a superseded citation of failed bytes cannot block a rework for ever (the old failure stays history; the honest note explains it). The gate card's `bound` and `delivered.commits` read the same set the close judges. A SPECS amendment recording the 12/03 + 12/02 tightenings in docs/journey-format-spec.md §7 F-AC18 stays a human act (the 12/03 tightening was code-only too).
